key_insight: A layerwise self-adaptive PINN with dual-phase optimization improves stability and accuracy for high-Reynolds multidimensional coupled Burgers' equations, especially when sharp shock fronts emerge.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a mesh-free alternative for resolving steep spatio-temporal gradients in nonlinear PDEs where conventional finite-difference and finite-element solvers become unstable or mesh-dependent.
method: Dynamically reweights physics residual, initial-condition, and boundary-condition losses during training.
Uses a layerwise self-adaptive weighting strategy to better balance constraints across network layers.
Applies a dual-phase optimization scheme and compares against standard PINN baselines with and without L-BFGS.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments on multidimensional coupled Burgers' equations show lower relative L2 error and improved capture of evolving shock fronts versus standard PINN variants.
watch_item: Performance may depend on careful tuning of adaptive weights and optimization stages, and the approach is validated here only on Burgers-type benchmark problems.
paper_title: MATLAB-Based Layerwise Self-Adaptive Physics-Informed Neural Network in Applications to Multidimensional Coupled Burgers' Equations with High Reynolds Numbers
